### `entasis_joint_break_metrics_t`

## Callback types

### `entasis_constraint_validate_fn`

validates custom descriptions on add, apply and awakening

```c
typedef entasis_status_t (ENTASIS_CALL *entasis_constraint_validate_fn)(void * user_context, entasis_constraint_type_id_t type_id, const void * description, uint32_t description_size);
```

| Parameter          | C type                         | Meaning                                  |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| `user_context`     | `void *`                       | borrowed registration state              |
| `type_id`          | `entasis_constraint_type_id_t` | owning registered ID                     |
| `description`      | `const void *`                 | read-only tightly packed f32 description |
| `description_size` | `uint32_t`                     | exact scalar description size            |

returns OK or a public failure status

### `entasis_constraint_kernel_fn`

runs a native batched constraint phase through the C ABI

```c
typedef void (ENTASIS_CALL *entasis_constraint_kernel_fn)(void * user_context, const entasis_constraint_kernel_view_t * view);
```

| Parameter      | C type                                     | Meaning                            |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------- |
| `user_context` | `void *`                                   | borrowed registration state        |
| `view`         | `const entasis_constraint_kernel_view_t *` | callback-local masked kernel views |

no return value. unwinding through the runtime is forbidden

### `entasis_joint_reaction_provider_fn`

reads physical impulses for one watched custom constraint lane

all views expire on return. do not retain pointers, mutate the world or unwind through the callback. return impulses about body centers of mass, not forces

```c
typedef entasis_status_t (ENTASIS_CALL *entasis_joint_reaction_provider_fn)(void * user_context, const entasis_joint_reaction_provider_input_t * input, entasis_joint_impulse_wrench_t * output);
```

| Parameter      | C type                                            | Meaning                                               |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `user_context` | `void *`                                          | borrowed provider state                               |
| `input`        | `const entasis_joint_reaction_provider_input_t *` | callback-local input record                           |
| `output`       | `entasis_joint_impulse_wrench_t *`                | four writable wrench slots, fill the first body_count |

returns OK or a public failure status. failure publishes no reaction from the bundle

### `entasis_constraint_body_view_t`

callback-local pointers to one eight-lane body bundle

every non-NULL target is 32-byte aligned. only fields declared by the registration are exposed. pointers expire at callback return. do not retain them or mutate read-only targets

### `entasis_constraint_kernel_view_t`

one pointer-based custom constraint kernel invocation

one invocation per native SIMD bundle and phase. sequential fallback invokes a single active lane in source order. leave every inactive lane unchanged, including prestep and impulse storage. pointers and access flags apply only during this callback. no ordinary world API reentry, exceptions or longjmp are permitted. caller state must support concurrent worker calls

Size `56`, alignment `8`

| Field                 | C type                                   | Meaning                                         |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `bodies`              | `const entasis_constraint_body_view_t *` | body_count views, not stable body IDs           |
| `body_count`          | `uint32_t`                               | constraint arity from one through four          |
| `phase`               | `entasis_constraint_kernel_phase_t`      | current kernel phase                            |
| `prestep`             | `entasis_f32x8_t *`                      | writable structure-of-arrays prestep fields     |
| `prestep_field_count` | `uint32_t`                               | number of eight-lane prestep fields             |
| `impulse_field_count` | `uint32_t`                               | number of eight-lane accumulated-impulse fields |
| `impulses`            | `entasis_f32x8_t *`                      | writable accumulated impulses                   |
| `active_mask`         | `const entasis_i32x8_t *`                | eight lanes: -1 active, 0 inactive              |
| `dt`                  | `float`                                  | substep duration                                |
| `inverse_dt`          | `float`                                  | reciprocal substep duration                     |

### `entasis_custom_constraint_registration_t`

copied per-world custom constraint registration

register before the first step and before adding any constraints. descriptors and callback pointers are copied before allocator calls. user state remains borrowed. registration preserves the native type range, body/prestep/impulse layouts and sleeping limits. invalid descriptors and allocation failure consume no ID

Size `96`, alignment `8`

| `struct_version`      | `uint32_t`                       | initialize to 1                                           |
| `type_id`             | `entasis_constraint_type_id_t`   | unused custom ID from 56 through 63                       |
| `body_count`          | `uint32_t`                       | constraint arity from one through four                    |
| `description_size`    | `uint32_t`                       | tightly packed f32 scalar bytes, positive and at most 256 |
| `prestep_bundle_size` | `uint32_t`                       | exactly eight times description_size                      |
| `impulse_bundle_size` | `uint32_t`                       | positive multiple of 32, at most 1024                     |
| `_reserved0`          | `uint32_t`                       | initialize to zero                                        |
| `initial_access`      | `entasis_body_access_mask_t[4]`  | per-body access. entries beyond body_count must be zero   |
| `solve_access`        | `entasis_body_access_mask_t[4]`  | per-body access. entries beyond body_count must be zero   |
| `user_context`        | `void *`                         | caller state borrowed until world destruction             |
| `validate`            | `entasis_constraint_validate_fn` | required scalar validation callback                       |
| `kernel`              | `entasis_constraint_kernel_fn`   | required prestep/warmstart/solve callback                 |
| `incremental_kernel`  | `entasis_constraint_kernel_fn`   | NULL reuses kernel for incremental updates                |

## Functions

Functions returning `entasis_status_t` return `ENTASIS_STATUS_OK` on success or a failure status. Operation-specific return behavior is documented with the function

### Constraint operations and targets

#### `entasis_servo_settings`

constructs exact built-in servo settings without allocation

allocation: none

```c
ENTASIS_API entasis_servo_settings_t ENTASIS_CALL entasis_servo_settings(float maximum_speed, float base_speed, float maximum_force);
```

| Parameter       | C type  | Meaning                                           |
| --------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `maximum_speed` | `float` | maximum correction speed                          |
| `base_speed`    | `float` | minimum correction speed used while error remains |
| `maximum_force` | `float` | maximum force the servo may apply                 |

returns the servo settings

#### `entasis_motor_settings`

constructs motor settings from maximum force and stable softness semantics

softness is zero for a rigid motor and increases as the motor becomes softer. allocation: none

```c
ENTASIS_API entasis_motor_settings_t ENTASIS_CALL entasis_motor_settings(float maximum_force, float softness);
```

| Parameter       | C type  | Meaning                           |
| --------------- | ------- | --------------------------------- |
| `maximum_force` | `float` | maximum force the motor may apply |
| `softness`      | `float` | motor softness                    |

returns the motor settings

| `world`      | `entasis_world_t *`                                | target world                                                                 |

| `state`      | `const entasis_global_constraint_target_state_t *` | required target state for the existing linear-servo or axis-lock kind        |
| `diagnostic` | `entasis_diagnostic_t *`                           | optional diagnostic output, or NULL when detailed failure data is not needed |

returns ENTASIS_STATUS_OK on success or the validation, handle, state or capacity failure

#### `entasis_fixed_stepper_update`

advances a world in bounded exact fixed steps and returns interpolation alpha

after success, alpha is the remaining accumulator fraction in [0, 1). a failed step leaves its time in the accumulator, but does not roll back physics already performed. inspect the failure before deciding whether the world can continue

```c
ENTASIS_API entasis_status_t ENTASIS_CALL entasis_fixed_stepper_update(entasis_fixed_stepper_t * stepper, entasis_world_t * world, float elapsed, uint32_t * out_steps, float * out_alpha, entasis_diagnostic_t * diagnostic);
```

| Parameter    | C type                      | Meaning                                                                      |
| ------------ | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `stepper`    | `entasis_fixed_stepper_t *` | caller-owned fixed-step accumulator                                          |
| `world`      | `entasis_world_t *`         | target world                                                                 |
| `elapsed`    | `float`                     | elapsed real time added to the accumulator in seconds                        |
| `out_steps`  | `uint32_t *`                | receives the number of fixed simulation steps performed                      |
| `out_alpha`  | `float *`                   | receives the remaining accumulator fraction after stepping                   |
| `diagnostic` | `entasis_diagnostic_t *`    | optional diagnostic output, or NULL when detailed failure data is not needed |

| `velocity_iterations`      | `int32_t` | velocity solve iterations per substep         |
| `fallback_batch_threshold` | `int32_t` | batch index reserved for fallback constraints |

```c
ENTASIS_API entasis_command_buffer_t ENTASIS_CALL entasis_command_buffer(const entasis_command_t * commands, uint64_t command_count, entasis_status_t * statuses, uint64_t status_capacity, entasis_body_handle_t * body_results, uint64_t body_result_capacity, entasis_static_handle_t * static_results, uint64_t static_result_capacity);
```

| Parameter                | C type                      | Meaning                                                |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `commands`               | `const entasis_command_t *` | input structural command array                         |
| `command_count`          | `uint64_t`                  | number of commands                                     |
| `statuses`               | `entasis_status_t *`        | caller-owned per-command status array                  |
| `status_capacity`        | `uint64_t`                  | number of entries available in the status array        |
| `body_results`           | `entasis_body_handle_t *`   | caller-owned body handle result array                  |
| `body_result_capacity`   | `uint64_t`                  | number of entries available in the body result array   |
| `static_results`         | `entasis_static_handle_t *` | caller-owned static handle result array                |
| `static_result_capacity` | `uint64_t`                  | number of entries available in the static result array |

returns the command buffer

#### `entasis_world_apply_commands`

applies caller-owned structural commands in exact input order after one capacity preflight

one combined capacity check covers all body and static additions. the operation commits a successful prefix and stops at the first failure. out_processed receives the first failing command index. add commands write handles into caller-selected result slots. commands cannot reference handles created by another command in the same buffer. allocation: the initial capacity check may grow world storage. ownership: owner thread only while the world is idle

```c
ENTASIS_API entasis_status_t ENTASIS_CALL entasis_world_apply_commands(entasis_world_t * world, const entasis_command_buffer_t * buffer, uint64_t * out_processed, entasis_diagnostic_t * diagnostic);
```

| Parameter       | C type                             | Meaning                                                                      |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `world`         | `entasis_world_t *`                | target world                                                                 |
| `buffer`        | `const entasis_command_buffer_t *` | caller-owned command buffer                                                  |
| `out_processed` | `uint64_t *`                       | receives the number of commands processed before the operation stopped       |
| `diagnostic`    | `entasis_diagnostic_t *`           | optional diagnostic output, or NULL when detailed failure data is not needed |

#### `entasis_world_apply_commands_global`

Availability: mixed64 builds with `ENTASIS_PRECISION_MIXED64=1`

executes an ordered command buffer with one f64 position per command

requires the owner thread and exclusive access to an idle world. position_count must equal buffer.command_count. add and apply commands use their ordinal position instead of the embedded float position. remove commands ignore the paired position, including nonfinite values. capacity for additions is admitted before execution. stops on the first failed command and preserves earlier mutations and results. buffers remain caller-owned and must not overlap

```c
ENTASIS_API entasis_status_t ENTASIS_CALL entasis_world_apply_commands_global(entasis_world_t * world, const entasis_command_buffer_t * buffer, const entasis_global_position_t * positions, uint64_t position_count, uint64_t * out_processed, entasis_diagnostic_t * diagnostic);
```

| Parameter        | C type                              | Meaning                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `world`          | `entasis_world_t *`                 | target world                                                                       |
| `buffer`         | `const entasis_command_buffer_t *`  | required command buffer and caller-owned result storage                            |
| `positions`      | `const entasis_global_position_t *` | one current-frame f64 position per command ordinal, required for a nonempty buffer |
| `position_count` | `uint64_t`                          | must equal buffer.command_count, including remove commands                         |
| `out_processed`  | `uint64_t *`                        | required completed-command count, initialized to zero before validation            |
| `diagnostic`     | `entasis_diagnostic_t *`            | optional diagnostic output, or NULL when detailed failure data is not needed       |

returns ENTASIS_STATUS_OK when all commands succeed or the first failure, with out_processed reporting the successful prefix

#### `entasis_world_export_global_states`

Availability: mixed64 builds with `ENTASIS_PRECISION_MIXED64=1`

copies selected body, static and target authoring states into caller-owned streams

requires an idle world or an active read phase. does not wake objects or allocate. streams execute in the fixed order bodies, statics, constraint targets, then kinematic targets. all capacities are checked before processing any record. repeated handles execute in selection order. a later failure preserves completed prefixes and stops later records. unwritten output remains unchanged. snapshots contain current-frame positions and borrowed shape identities, without solver/contact history, sleep counters or execution phase state

```c
ENTASIS_API entasis_status_t ENTASIS_CALL entasis_world_export_global_states(entasis_world_t * world, const entasis_global_state_selection_t * selection, entasis_global_state_snapshot_t * snapshot, entasis_global_state_counts_t * out_counts, entasis_diagnostic_t * diagnostic);
```

| Parameter    | C type                                     | Meaning                                                                      |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `world`      | `entasis_world_t *`                        | target world                                                                 |
| `selection`  | `const entasis_global_state_selection_t *` | required live-handle arrays with a non-NULL pointer for each nonzero count   |
| `snapshot`   | `entasis_global_state_snapshot_t *`        | required disjoint output streams, each capacity covering its selected count  |
| `out_counts` | `entasis_global_state_counts_t *`          | required per-stream written counts, initialized to zero before validation    |
| `diagnostic` | `entasis_diagnostic_t *`                   | optional diagnostic output, or NULL when detailed failure data is not needed |

returns ENTASIS_STATUS_OK when all selected records succeed or the first failure, with per-stream completed counts

#### `entasis_world_apply_global_states`

Availability: mixed64 builds with `ENTASIS_PRECISION_MIXED64=1`

applies selected body, static and target authoring states in stream order

requires the owner thread and exclusive access to an idle world. normal storage growth may allocate and successful mutation invalidates borrowed direct views. streams execute in the fixed order bodies, statics, constraint targets, then kinematic targets. all capacities are checked before processing any record. repeated handles execute in selection order. a later failure preserves completed prefixes and stops later records. mutations are not rolled back as a group, and awakening side effects may remain on a failed record. input streams and selections must be disjoint and remain valid until return. identities must already exist in this world. translate saved positions after an origin shift before applying them

```c
ENTASIS_API entasis_status_t ENTASIS_CALL entasis_world_apply_global_states(entasis_world_t * world, const entasis_global_state_selection_t * selection, const entasis_global_state_snapshot_t * snapshot, entasis_awakening_policy_t awakening, entasis_body_control_wake_t target_wake, entasis_global_state_counts_t * out_counts, entasis_diagnostic_t * diagnostic);
```

| Parameter     | C type                                     | Meaning                                                                        |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `world`       | `entasis_world_t *`                        | target world                                                                   |
| `selection`   | `const entasis_global_state_selection_t *` | required destination live-handle arrays, without cross-world remapping         |
| `snapshot`    | `const entasis_global_state_snapshot_t *`  | required caller-owned input streams, each capacity covering its selected count |
| `awakening`   | `entasis_awakening_policy_t`               | awakening policy for static state applications                                 |
| `target_wake` | `entasis_body_control_wake_t`              | wake policy for present kinematic target applications                          |
| `out_counts`  | `entasis_global_state_counts_t *`          | required per-stream applied counts, initialized to zero before validation      |
| `diagnostic`  | `entasis_diagnostic_t *`                   | optional diagnostic output, or NULL when detailed failure data is not needed   |

returns ENTASIS_STATUS_OK when all selected records succeed or the first failure, with per-stream completed counts

Availability: mixed64 builds with `ENTASIS_PRECISION_MIXED64=1`

sets or clears a custom constraint type's reaction reader and position frame

requires the owner thread and exclusive access to an idle world with joint breaks enabled. the type must already be registered and have no watches. a non-NULL provider must match the registered type's position frame. copies the descriptor on success and borrows its user state until replacement, clearing or world disposal. rejection preserves the previous provider

```c
ENTASIS_API entasis_status_t ENTASIS_CALL entasis_constraint_set_reaction_provider_position_space(entasis_world_t * world, entasis_constraint_type_id_t type_id, const entasis_joint_reaction_provider_t * provider, entasis_constraint_position_space_t position_space, entasis_diagnostic_t * diagnostic);
```

| Parameter        | C type                                      | Meaning                                                                                 |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `world`          | `entasis_world_t *`                         | idle world with joint breaks enabled                                                    |
| `type_id`        | `entasis_constraint_type_id_t`              | custom type registered in this world                                                    |
| `provider`       | `const entasis_joint_reaction_provider_t *` | descriptor to copy, with caller-owned callback code and state. NULL clears the provider |
| `position_space` | `entasis_constraint_position_space_t`       | valid position frame, which must match the registered type when installing a provider   |
| `diagnostic`     | `entasis_diagnostic_t *`                    | optional diagnostic output                                                              |

returns ENTASIS_STATUS_OK on success or the validation, handle, state or capacity failure
